videos.title: Computer networks overview
videos.concept: A laptop request travels through a switch, router and ISP to a server and back, showing end systems, links, packets and protocols.
videos.realWorld: A campus LAN 10.10.0.0/16 reaching a public web server through an ISP and an IXP.
videos.tools: ping 8.8.8.8 and tracert 8.8.8.8 in a terminal

videos.title: Data journey through the OSI layers
videos.concept: A web request moves down the seven OSI layers on the sender, across the wire, and back up on the receiver, each layer doing one job.
videos.realWorld: A browser on 192.168.1.10 loading a page from a server through a home switch and router.
videos.tools: Wireshark packet details pane expanding Ethernet, IP, TCP and HTTP

videos.title: Encapsulation and headers
videos.concept: Application data gains a TCP header, then an IP header, then an Ethernet header and trailer, becoming a segment, a packet and a frame.
videos.realWorld: One web request frame with real values: source and destination MACs, 192.168.1.10 to 93.184.216.34, TCP port 80.
videos.tools: Wireshark frame bytes view with each header highlighted

videos.title: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN in practice
videos.concept: Network scale grows from a Bluetooth PAN to an office LAN, a city MAN and a WAN between cities, with the link technology changing at each step.
videos.realWorld: A company with an office LAN 10.1.0.0/16 linked to a branch 10.2.0.0/16 over an MPLS WAN.

videos.title: Topologies in real offices
videos.concept: Bus, ring, star, mesh and tree compared by what happens when one link or node fails.
videos.realWorld: A star of access switches uplinked to a core switch in an office building, with a partial mesh between core routers.
videos.tools: show cdp neighbors on a Cisco switch

videos.title: Physical layer overview
videos.concept: Bits become electrical signals on copper, light in fiber or radio waves in air, limited by bandwidth, noise and distance.
videos.realWorld: A home fiber ONT feeding a router, with Cat6 to a PC and Wi-Fi to a phone.
videos.tools: ethtool eth0 showing link speed and duplex

videos.title: Transmission media and cabling
videos.concept: UTP twisted pairs, coaxial cable, single mode and multimode fiber compared by bandwidth, distance and interference.
videos.realWorld: Structured cabling in an office: Cat6 horizontal runs to a patch panel and a fiber backbone between floors.
videos.tools: A cable tester reading and ethtool link speed

videos.title: Signals, encoding and attenuation
videos.concept: Bits 10110 shown as NRZ and Manchester waveforms, then the signal weakens and picks up noise along a long cable until a repeater regenerates it.
videos.realWorld: The 100 m Ethernet run limit, and why longer links use switches or fiber.
videos.tools: Oscilloscope style waveform with dB loss values

videos.title: Multiplexing: FDM and TDM
videos.concept: Several users share a link: FDM gives each a frequency band, TDM gives each a time slot, and statistical TDM gives slots on demand.
videos.realWorld: FDM in cable TV and DSL, TDM in T1 and E1 lines, and statistical multiplexing on every Ethernet uplink.

videos.title: Circuit vs packet switching
videos.concept: A circuit reserves a path before data flows, while packets share links and queue independently at each hop.
videos.realWorld: A classic telephone call compared with VoIP packets crossing an ISP network.

videos.title: Data link layer overview
videos.concept: Packets become frames moved one hop at a time using MAC addressing, error detection and access control.
videos.realWorld: Frames crossing an office switch from 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E to the default gateway MAC.
videos.tools: arp -a and the Wireshark filter eth.addr

videos.title: Framing and CRC
videos.concept: A frame gets a preamble, addresses, type, payload and FCS. The sender computes the CRC by XOR division and the receiver recomputes it to detect errors.
videos.realWorld: Ethernet FCS dropping a corrupted frame on a switch port and raising its error counter.

videos.title: Sliding window ARQ
videos.concept: Go-Back-N resends from the lost frame onward, Selective Repeat resends only the lost frame, and the window slides on each ACK.
videos.realWorld: Reliable delivery on a long satellite link, and the same idea inside TCP.
videos.tools: Wireshark view of duplicate ACKs and retransmissions

videos.title: CSMA/CD and Ethernet
videos.concept: Stations sense the wire, transmit, detect a collision, send a jam signal and back off for a random time.
videos.realWorld: Legacy hub based Ethernet, and why full duplex switches removed collisions.
videos.tools: show interfaces showing 0 collisions on a full duplex port

videos.title: Switch MAC learning
videos.concept: A switch learns source MACs per port, floods unknown destinations and then forwards only to the correct port.
videos.realWorld: Four PCs on a Cisco access switch in an office filling its MAC table.

videos.title: VLANs and 802.1Q trunking
videos.concept: One switch carries separate broadcast domains, and an 802.1Q tag on the trunk keeps VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 traffic apart.
videos.realWorld: HR on VLAN 10 and Engineering on VLAN 20 across two floors, joined by a trunk and routed by a layer 3 switch.
videos.tools: switchport mode trunk and show vlan brief

videos.title: IP addressing overview
videos.concept: IPv4 addresses split into network and host parts, and routers use the network part to move packets between networks.
videos.realWorld: A home 192.168.1.0/24 network behind one public address from the ISP.
videos.tools: ipconfig or ip addr showing address, mask and gateway

videos.title: IPv4 addressing and subnetting
videos.concept: 192.168.10.0/24 splits into four /26 subnets by borrowing two host bits, shown in binary with network, host and broadcast ranges.
videos.realWorld: A small office giving separate subnets to staff, servers, guests and printers.
videos.tools: Binary mask panel and ip addr output

videos.title: VLSM office design
videos.concept: Allocate the largest subnet first: from 10.0.0.0/24 give 100 hosts a /25, 50 hosts a /26, 20 hosts a /27 and the router link a /30.
videos.realWorld: A branch office address plan with sales, IT, guest Wi-Fi and a WAN link.
videos.tools: show ip route connected on the branch router

videos.title: NAT on a home router
videos.concept: PAT rewrites private 192.168.1.10:51000 to public 203.0.113.5:40001 and records the mapping so replies return to the correct device.
videos.realWorld: Three home devices sharing one ISP address, and CGNAT at the ISP.

videos.title: ICMP, ping and traceroute
videos.concept: Ping uses echo request and reply, and traceroute raises the TTL by one each round so that each router returns Time Exceeded.
videos.realWorld: A support engineer locating a fault between a campus gateway and an ISP router.
videos.tools: ping 8.8.8.8, traceroute 8.8.8.8 and the Wireshark filter icmp

videos.title: IPv6 basics
videos.concept: 128 bit addresses written in hex, the compression rules, global, link-local and multicast types, and SLAAC through Router Advertisements.
videos.realWorld: A dual stack ISP handing a /56 prefix to a home router.

videos.title: Routing overview
videos.concept: Forwarding moves a packet using the table, routing builds the table, and longest prefix match picks the route.
videos.realWorld: An enterprise router choosing between a connected LAN, an OSPF route and a default route to the ISP.

videos.title: Static vs dynamic routing
videos.concept: Static routes are typed by hand and stay until changed, while dynamic protocols learn routes and reroute when a link fails.
videos.realWorld: A branch with a static default route compared with a campus core running OSPF.

videos.title: Distance vector and RIP
videos.concept: Routers exchange distance tables with neighbors and apply Bellman-Ford, and count to infinity appears after a link failure until the 16 hop limit.
videos.realWorld: RIP in a small legacy network, with split horizon preventing loops.

videos.title: OSPF link state routing
videos.concept: Routers form neighbors, flood LSAs, build the same map and run Dijkstra to compute shortest paths.
videos.realWorld: A campus with an area 0 backbone and an area 1 for one building, using cost based on bandwidth.

videos.title: BGP and internet routing
videos.concept: Autonomous systems advertise prefixes with AS paths, and routers choose by policy rather than shortest distance.
videos.realWorld: A company in AS 64512 multihomed to two ISPs, with those ISPs peering at an IXP.

videos.title: Transport layer overview
videos.concept: Port numbers deliver data to the right process, with UDP being fast and simple and TCP being reliable.
videos.realWorld: A laptop running a browser, a video call and DNS at once, separated by port numbers.

videos.title: UDP vs TCP
videos.concept: UDP sends datagrams with an 8 byte header and no setup, while TCP sets up a connection, numbers bytes and retransmits losses.
videos.realWorld: DNS and video calls on UDP compared with web and file transfer on TCP.

videos.title: TCP three-way handshake
videos.concept: SYN seq=1000, SYN-ACK seq=5000 ack=1001 and ACK ack=5001 exchange initial sequence numbers before data flows.
videos.realWorld: A browser opening a connection to a web server on port 443.

videos.title: TCP flow control
videos.concept: The receiver advertises rwnd, the sender limits unacknowledged bytes to it, and a zero window pauses the sender until a window update.
videos.realWorld: A fast server sending to a slow phone, and Linux socket buffer tuning.
videos.tools: Wireshark TCP window field and tcp.analysis.zero_window

videos.title: TCP congestion control
videos.concept: cwnd doubles each RTT in slow start, grows by one MSS per RTT in congestion avoidance, and halves after three duplicate ACKs.
videos.realWorld: A bulk download sharing a congested ISP link, and CUBIC on Linux servers.

videos.title: Application layer overview
videos.concept: Applications talk through protocols using client-server or peer-to-peer models on top of TCP or UDP.
videos.realWorld: Opening a website uses DHCP, DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP in sequence.

videos.title: DNS resolution
videos.concept: A recursive resolver walks the root, TLD and authoritative servers to turn www.example.com into an IP address, then caches it for the TTL.
videos.realWorld: A home router or 8.8.8.8 acting as the resolver, with A, AAAA, CNAME and MX records.

videos.title: HTTP and HTTPS request
videos.concept: A client sends a method, path and headers, and the server returns a status code, headers and body, all inside TLS for HTTPS.
videos.realWorld: A browser loading a page from a load balanced web server with cookies and cache headers.
videos.tools: curl -I https://example.com and the browser DevTools Network tab

videos.title: DHCP DORA
videos.concept: Discover, Offer, Request and Ack give a new client an IP address, mask, gateway and DNS server for a lease time.
videos.realWorld: A laptop joining office Wi-Fi, with a DHCP server and a relay on the router.
videos.tools: ipconfig /renew and the Wireshark filter dhcp

videos.title: Email: SMTP and IMAP
videos.concept: The sender's client submits through SMTP, servers relay using MX records, and the receiver reads over IMAP or POP3.
videos.realWorld: A webmail user emailing a company mailbox hosted on another provider.

videos.title: Network security overview
videos.concept: The CIA triad maps to threats at each layer and to defenses such as encryption, firewalls and monitoring.
videos.realWorld: A company network with a firewall, a DMZ, a VPN and an IDS.

videos.title: Symmetric and asymmetric crypto
videos.concept: AES uses one shared key and is fast, RSA and ECDH use key pairs, and hybrid systems exchange a session key and then encrypt with it.
videos.realWorld: HTTPS using ECDHE to agree on an AES session key.
videos.tools: openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 showing the cipher

videos.title: TLS handshake
videos.concept: ClientHello, ServerHello, certificate, key share and Finished messages establish keys and prove the server identity.
videos.realWorld: A browser validating a bank's certificate chain up to a trusted root CA.
videos.tools: openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 and the Wireshark filter tls.handshake

videos.title: Firewalls and ACLs
videos.concept: An ACL checks rules from the top with an implicit deny at the end, and a stateful firewall allows replies using its connection table.
videos.realWorld: A DMZ web server allowed on TCP 443 from the internet, with the inside LAN blocked.
videos.tools: access-list 101 permit tcp any host 203.0.113.10 eq 443

videos.title: VPN tunnels
videos.concept: IPsec encrypts the original packet and carries it inside a new IP header between two gateways.
videos.realWorld: Site-to-site IPsec between head office and a branch, and a remote access VPN for staff.

videos.title: Common attacks and defenses
videos.concept: ARP spoofing, DNS poisoning, DDoS and MITM shown as an attack path that a matching defense then blocks.
videos.realWorld: Dynamic ARP Inspection on a switch, DNSSEC, and a scrubbing service at an ISP.

videos.title: Wireless and mobile overview
videos.concept: Radio is shared, lossy and mobile, so wireless links need different access control and handover.
videos.realWorld: A phone moving from home Wi-Fi to 5G, and sensors reporting over Zigbee.

videos.title: Wi-Fi and CSMA/CA
videos.concept: A station senses the channel, waits DIFS plus a random backoff, and optional RTS and CTS solve the hidden terminal problem before data and ACK.
videos.realWorld: A crowded office floor with access points on channels 1, 6 and 11.

videos.title: Cellular handover
videos.concept: A phone reports signal strength, the source base station hands over to the target cell, and the core moves the data path without dropping the session.
videos.realWorld: A 4G phone in a moving car switching eNodeB cells, with the MME and S-GW in the core.

videos.title: Bluetooth, IoT and MQTT
videos.concept: Sensors publish to topics on an MQTT broker, and subscribers receive only the topics they asked for.
videos.realWorld: A smart factory where a temperature sensor publishes to factory/line1/temp and BLE beacons feed a gateway.

videos.title: Modern networking overview
videos.concept: Networks are now software controlled, virtualized and automated from the data center to the edge.
videos.realWorld: An app deployed in a cloud VPC behind a load balancer and a CDN.

videos.title: SDN: control and data planes
videos.concept: A central controller computes flows and installs them through OpenFlow, while switches only match and forward.
videos.realWorld: A data center using an SDN controller to isolate tenants.

videos.title: Cloud VPC networking
videos.concept: A VPC 10.0.0.0/16 holds public and private subnets, with route tables, an internet gateway, a NAT gateway and security groups.
videos.realWorld: A three tier app with a load balancer, app servers and a private database.

videos.title: CDN and caching
videos.concept: DNS steers the user to a nearby edge, a hit is served from cache, and a miss fetches from the origin and stores the object for its TTL.
videos.realWorld: A video site serving users in India from a Mumbai edge instead of a US origin.
videos.tools: curl -I showing X-Cache and Age headers

videos.title: Leaf-spine data centers
videos.concept: Every leaf connects to every spine, giving equal hop counts and ECMP load sharing between any two servers.
videos.realWorld: A 40 rack data center with 100 GbE uplinks replacing an older three tier design.
videos.tools: show ip route showing ECMP next hops

videos.title: QoS and traffic shaping
videos.concept: Packets are classified and marked with DSCP, queued by priority, and shaped with a token bucket to the link rate.
videos.realWorld: VoIP marked DSCP EF and prioritized over backups on a branch WAN link.
